inlinearray-fixed-buffer-layout.title: Embed fixed-size buffers with InlineArray
inlinearray-fixed-buffer-layout.short: Represent contiguous fixed-length elements inside a value type
inlinearray-fixed-buffer-layout.summary: InlineArrayAttribute gives a struct a fixed number of contiguous elements with array-like indexing and span access.
inlinearray-fixed-buffer-layout.why: It can represent small fixed buffers without a separate array, which is useful for interop and allocation-sensitive code.
inlinearray-fixed-buffer-layout.tips: Embedding large buffers increases value-type copy costs, so keep sizes and usage deliberately bounded.

static-abstract-generic-algorithms.title: Build generic algorithms with static abstract members
static-abstract-generic-algorithms.short: Call static operations and constants through generic constraints
static-abstract-generic-algorithms.summary: Static abstract interface members let generic code invoke type-specific static operations through an interface constraint.
static-abstract-generic-algorithms.why: They enable type-safe reusable algorithms such as generic math without duplicating implementations or relying on dynamic dispatch.
static-abstract-generic-algorithms.tips: Constrain only the operations the algorithm needs and avoid generalizing simple code without a real reuse benefit.

iexceptionhandler-centralized-errors.title: Centralize ASP.NET Core errors with IExceptionHandler
iexceptionhandler-centralized-errors.short: Convert unhandled exceptions into consistent HTTP responses
iexceptionhandler-centralized-errors.summary: IExceptionHandler implements ASP.NET Core exception handling as a service and can produce consistent ProblemDetails responses.
iexceptionhandler-centralized-errors.why: It avoids repeating the same try/catch logic across endpoints while centralizing logging and external error contracts.
iexceptionhandler-centralized-errors.tips: Do not turn expected validation failures into exceptions, and never expose internal exception details to clients.

quic-stream-lifetime-model.title: Understand System.Net.Quic connection and stream lifetimes
quic-stream-lifetime-model.short: Use independent QUIC streams over one connection
quic-stream-lifetime-model.summary: QUIC supports multiple bidirectional or unidirectional streams over a connection, each performing independent asynchronous I/O.
quic-stream-lifetime-model.why: Separating connection and stream lifetimes helps design correct cancellation, completion, and multiplexed communication behavior.
quic-stream-lifetime-model.tips: Check QUIC support on the target platform and asynchronously dispose both the connection and every stream.

no-gc-region-latency-window.title: Use a No GC Region for a short latency-critical window
no-gc-region-latency-window.short: Reserve an allocation budget to temporarily avoid GC pauses
no-gc-region-latency-window.summary: GC.TryStartNoGCRegion is an advanced facility for avoiding collections during a bounded section when enough allocation budget is available.
no-gc-region-latency-window.why: In specialized latency-sensitive work it can reduce GC pause variability for a short, measured interval.
no-gc-region-latency-window.tips: Do not use it as a general optimization; measure allocation requirements and always handle failure and EndNoGCRegion correctly.

exception-filter-selective-handling.title: Select exceptions before catch with exception filters
exception-filter-selective-handling.short: Use catch when to handle only matching exception states
exception-filter-selective-handling.summary: Exception filters evaluate a condition before entering a catch body, allowing the same exception type to be handled differently by state.
exception-filter-selective-handling.why: They express selective handling without catching and rethrowing exceptions that should continue along their original exception path.
exception-filter-selective-handling.tips: Keep filters simple and avoid side effects or operations that can fail while evaluating the condition.

socket-backpressure-unbounded-send-queue.title: Do not build an unbounded Socket send queue
socket-backpressure-unbounded-send-queue.short: Apply capacity limits and backpressure to outbound work
socket-backpressure-unbounded-send-queue.summary: Starting asynchronous sends without a bound when producers outrun the network can accumulate unfinished operations and retained buffers.
socket-backpressure-unbounded-send-queue.why: A bounded design prevents memory and pending-work growth from cascading under sustained load.
socket-backpressure-unbounded-send-queue.tips: Use a bounded Channel or similar queue and explicitly choose whether full capacity should wait, drop, or reject work.

reflection-activator-hot-path.title: Avoid repeated Activator.CreateInstance on hot paths
reflection-activator-hot-path.short: Build and reuse object factories when the target type is stable
reflection-activator-hot-path.summary: Repeated Activator or reflection lookup for the same type adds overhead when object creation occurs at high frequency.
reflection-activator-hot-path.why: Caching an appropriate factory can remove repeated reflection work from measured hot paths.
reflection-activator-hot-path.tips: Measure before optimizing, and choose a factory strategy that does not depend on dynamic code when AOT compatibility is required.

unity-object-pooling-spawn-churn.title: Replace Unity spawn/despawn churn with object pooling
unity-object-pooling-spawn-churn.short: Reuse frequently spawned GameObjects instead of repeatedly creating them
unity-object-pooling-spawn-churn.summary: Rapid Instantiate and Destroy cycles for projectiles or effects can increase creation cost and garbage-collection pressure.
unity-object-pooling-spawn-churn.why: Pooling reusable objects can reduce per-frame allocations and variability in frequently executed gameplay paths.
unity-object-pooling-spawn-churn.tips: Reset all reusable state on release and avoid retaining a pool much larger than the actual concurrency requirement.

aspnetcore-request-body-buffering-cost.title: Avoid unconditional ASP.NET Core request-body buffering
aspnetcore-request-body-buffering-cost.short: Buffer request bodies only when they genuinely need to be reread
aspnetcore-request-body-buffering-cost.summary: Always reading the full request body or enabling buffering can increase memory or temporary-storage pressure for large requests.
aspnetcore-request-body-buffering-cost.why: When the body can be processed once, preserving streaming avoids unnecessary buffering proportional to request size.
aspnetcore-request-body-buffering-cost.tips: Reserve rereading for requirements such as signature validation and combine it with explicit request-size limits.
